numerical_failure.observed_behavior: tz_localize silently wrapped an out-of-range UTC int64 instant or returned the NaT sentinel instead of reporting an out-of-bounds conversion; in the zoneinfo fallback path, both UTC bounds stayed NaT after a failed round-trip check, and the caller either treated the wall time as a DST gap or returned NaT under nonexistent='NaT'.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: When the UTC instant is unrepresentable (out of the supported datetime bounds), tz_localize (and underlying tz_localize_to_utc paths) should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime rather than wrapping int64 or returning NaT; for nonexistent='NaT', it should still raise OutOfBoundsDatetime for this out-of-range case.
trigger_conditions: Execution/path: tz_localize_to_utc where the derived UTC instant is out of range for the int64 representation
Zone: America/New_York (DST zone where the described failing DST/out-of-range combination occurs)
Condition: nonexistent='NaT' leads to silent NaT before the fix

Code regression condition (zoneinfo fallback): _get_utc_bounds derived candidate UTC instants with bare `val - delta` (un-checked subtraction), so a wrapped candidate fails the round-trip check and leaves both bounds as NaT

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ValueError: ... is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time

oracle_clues: PR#66698 describes the regression: zoneinfo fallback in `_get_utc_bounds` derived candidate UTC instants with bare `val - delta`, unlike the cached path which uses `checked_sub`; wrapped candidate fails the fallback's round-trip check so both bounds stay NaT.

Before/after oracle for the default path includes: before `ValueError: ... is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time`; after `OutOfBoundsDatetime: Converting ... overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807`.
Before/after oracle for nonexistent='NaT' includes: before `NaT` (silent); after `OutOfBoundsDatetime`.

Relevant implementation evidence: tzconversion.pyx shows `_get_utc_bounds` changed from `v_left = val - delta0` / `v_right = val - delta1` to using `checked_sub` in that branch (with comments about GH#65733 wrapped int64 failing round-trip and leaving bounds NaT).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: UTC/local timestamp values near/outside pandas Timestamp representable range: past Timestamp.max and around the NaT sentinel (including one below the minimum representable value)
category_specific_evidence: GH#65733: a candidate that wrapped int64 fails the round-trip check and leaves both UTC bounds as NaT; caller treats it as a nonexistent time instead of raising OutOfBoundsDatetime. (tzconversion.pyx: _get_utc_bounds uses checked_sub and notes round-trip below leaves both bounds NaT).

PR#66698 repro: ts = pd.Timestamp("2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807") ; ts.tz_localize("America/New_York") before: ValueError ... nonexistent time; after: OutOfBoundsDatetime: "Converting ... overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807".
PR#66698 repro: ts.tz_localize("America/New_York", nonexistent="NaT") before: NaT (silent); after: OutOfBoundsDatetime.

commit: GH#65733 fixed: zoneinfo fallback subtracted candidate offsets without bounds check; wrapped candidate fails round-trip check so both bounds stayed NaT; reported as "a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time" or silently returned NaT under nonexistent="NaT".
commit: also describes fixed-offset/machine-local loops shifting with a bare subtraction; two or more values near Timestamp.min/max came back in year -2262 (wrap) instead of raising.
test_diff (tzconversion bounds/sentinel logic): _shift_to_utc uses _shift_to_utc(v, delta, creso) and if result[i] == NPY_NAT raises out-of-bounds via raise_out_of_bounds(v, BS_UNDERFLOW, creso).

test_diff: GH#66550 shift landing exactly on the NaT sentinel is one below the minimum representable value, so it underflows; tz_localize should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with match "underflows past" for dti built from np.array([-(2**63) + 9*3600*10**9], dtype="i8").view("M8[ns]").

test_diff: GH#65733 overflow past last cached transition wraps instead of reporting out-of-bounds UTC instant; test expects OutOfBoundsDatetime("overflows past") when tz_localize is called with kwargs in [{}, {"nonexistent":"NaT"}, {"nonexistent":"shift_forward"}] on dti = DatetimeIndex([Timestamp(Timestamp.max._value - 2*3600*10**9)]).
reproduction_risks: Repro outcomes depend on which tz_localize path is used (zoneinfo fallback vs fixed-offset/use_tzlocal/use_fixed loops), since the described bug manifests as int64 wrapping/NaT results in those specific branches.

Need to choose timestamps near pandas Timestamp representable boundaries (Timestamp.max/min and the NaT sentinel); the evidence specifies concrete boundary-adjacent values (e.g., 2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807 and Timestamp.max._value - 2*3600*10**9; and one-below-min via the i8 pattern).
The observed behavior changes with the nonexistent= parameter (e.g., nonexistent="NaT" caused silent NaT before the fix, but should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime after).

provenance.value: tz_localize can overflow the UTC instant and silently wrap int64 or return NaT, instead of reporting an out-of-bounds conversion error. In the zoneinfo fallback path, the candidate UTC instants fail a round-trip check so both bounds stay NaT; the caller then reports an ordinary wall time as a DST gap before the fix, and returns NaT silently under nonexistent='NaT'.

When the UTC instant is unrepresentable (out of the supported datetime bounds), tz_localize (and the underlying tz_localize_to_utc paths) should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime rather than wrapping int64 or returning the NaT sentinel. For nonexistent='NaT', it should still raise OutOfBoundsDatetime rather than silently returning NaT for this out-of-range case.
